mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full reconditioned or rebuilt Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC engine typically costs between £5,500 and £12,000 for the unit itself, depending on the level of rebuild and whether upgraded components are included.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your AJ133 engine. Listen for a distinct rattling or clattering noise from the engine bay for 1-3 seconds on a cold start. Look for sudden loss of power, check engine lights, or misfire codes if the chain has already stretched or jumped.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely, given the high retained values and enthusiast demand for the L494 5.0 SC models. A rebuilt AJ133 engine with upgraded metal tensioners and aluminium coolant pipes can extend the vehicle's life significantly. For vehicles valued over £15,000, a warranted reconditioned engine protects your investment far better than a cheap used unit.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the 5.0 SC and the SVR engine in the Range Rover Sport?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both variants use the legendary 5.0-litre supercharged V8 architecture. The standard 5.0 SC (AJ133) produces 510-550 PS and focuses on luxury performance. The SVR (AJ133S) produces 550-575 PS, featuring a higher-output tune, specific cooling calibration, and reinforced internal mapping for track use.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straightforward supply and fit of a reconditioned AJ133 engine typically takes 4 to 6 days at a specialist workshop. This allows time for proper bedding-in procedures, supercharger calibration, fluid checks, and a thorough road test to ensure the V8 powertrain is performing flawlessly.

commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC is celebrated for its thunderous V8 soundtrack and effortless acceleration, but the AJ133 engine requires vigilant maintenance. The AJ133 5.0L Supercharged V8 dominates replacement demand for this high-performance variant. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components, such as revised metal timing chain tensioners and aluminium coolant crossover pipes, addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC AJ133 Rattles on Startup
problems.rootCause: Early plastic timing chain tensioners and guides degrade and lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack. If ignored, the chain can skip teeth on the camshaft sprockets, causing valves to contact pistons and resulting in catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chains, upgraded metal tensioners, guides, and VVT hardware before failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended if caught early (audible rattle on cold start but no running issues).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the chain has already jumped timing, causing internal valve/piston damage.

problems.recommendation: If your Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC exhibits a timing chain rattle on cold start, do not drive the vehicle-invest in a preventative specialist chain replacement immediately to save the engine. If the engine has already jumped timing, suffered hydrolock from a coolant leak, or developed a bottom-end knock, a full reconditioned replacement is the only reliable long-term investment.

problems.group: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks & Supercharger Coupler Wear
problems.h4: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks & Supercharger Coupler Wear - Why the Range Rover Sport 5.0 SC Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The plastic coolant crossover pipes located in the engine valley become brittle under extreme heat cycling, leading to sudden coolant loss. Additionally, the supercharger nose coupler can wear out, causing a distinct rattling noise and potential oil contamination of the drive belts.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace plastic pipes with upgraded aluminium components, flush system, and replace supercharger coupler.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early and there is no secondary internal engine damage from overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if severe coolant loss has caused the engine to overheat and warp the cylinder heads.
